text:
jordan (support): Heads up — Acme reporting intermittent 502/504s on hosted streaming endpoints since ~09:12 PST. Pattern: partial stream then a 502 close. Sample request id: req-7f9a2b. ~20% of long streams (>45s) affected. Posting the curl they used and response snippet.

kevin (acme-customer): Yep, confirmed on our side. Happens for long chat completions in us-west-2 and us-east-1. No client disconnects from our logs, just abrupt 502 mid-stream.

jordan (support): curl they ran:
```
curl -v --http2 "https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-stream","prompt":"long conversation...","stream":true}'
```
response ended with:
```
HTTP/2 502
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream connect error or disconnect"}
```

mia (SRE): On it. Can you paste the edge ids / x-request-id or x-edge-request headers from the failed requests? Any deploys around that window? Also please run a trace curl with an X-Trace header so we can correlate.

jordan (support): Sample headers from one failed req:
`x-edge-id: gw-36b2`
`x-request-id: req-7f9a2b`
`x-auth-proxy-id: ap-12f4`
No customer-side deploys. We had a config push to auth-proxy two hours earlier (rollout v2.14.1).

mia (SRE): Thanks. Quick grep of gw-36b2 logs shows repeated upstream reset reasons during the window: `upstream reset: connection failure` and `h2.rst_stream: INTERNAL_ERROR`. Also auth-proxy ap-12f4 has a spike in 502 responses to edge (auth cache queue depth high). Suspect auth-proxy worker saturation + h2 keepalive mismatch.

sam (eng-runtime): That matches a known mode where auth proxy backpressure causes upstream to RST streams, which Envoy surfaces as 502. If auth-proxy returns early on heartbeat checks we see partial streams close. Can you collect a short tcpdump or envoy access log lines for a couple of req ids?

jordan (support): Pasted two access lines for req-7f9a2b and req-9c3d11:
`[gw-36b2] "POST /v1/stream" 502 UH 0/1/45000/45002 1234 "upstream reset: rst_stream" "ap-12f4"`
`[gw-36b2] "POST /v1/stream" 504 UO 0/0/90000/90005 4567 "upstream timeout" "ap-12f4"`

mia (SRE): I can repro locally by simulating auth-proxy queue saturation. Metrics: auth_cache.queue_depth peaked at 128 and auth-proxy worker threads hit max. h2 connection window behavior looks flaky when auth-proxy stalls. I'm going to roll a temporary mitigation: increase auth-proxy worker pool, add a 2s circuit for slow auth lookups to fail-open for streaming tenant routes, and bump edge downstream timeouts to 95s.

jordan (support): I'll notify Acme and apply tenant-level routing policy fallback while we patch.

deploy-bot: deploy finished — rolled auth-proxy ap-12f4 back to v2.13.9 on us-west-2 (2024-06-21T09:35:00Z).

sam (eng-runtime): Follow-up plan: 1) add rate-limited KV cache for auth lookups, 2) tune h2 keepalive/flow-control on edge nodes, 3) add telemetry to catch auth backpressure early. I'll file an RFC and link it here.

mia (SRE): After rollback + temporary timeout bump, error rate for Acme streams dropped from ~20% -> ~3%. Customer reports immediate improvement :thumbsup:.

jordan (support): Filed internal ticket INC-2024-3712 and emailed Acme with mitigation steps and ETA for a permanent fix. Will update when RFC is in. Thanks everyone.
